Insert: Autonomous gamebots form and join realm guilds (see docs/BOT-GUILDS.md), and players can /ginvite them. False keeps every gamebot guildless; saved memberships are kept.
Autonomous gamebots get a personality and traits that tilt town breaks, goals, dungeons, camps and chattiness (see docs/BOT-PERSONALITIES.md).
Autonomous gamebots say pre-written, period lines in their own writing style (docs/bot-voices/DESIGN.md).

Server life: autonomous gamebots of your realm remember grouping with you, your rezzes and rude words; they greet you by name, thank you for an old rez, answer you by name, mention you in /faction now and then, and stay cool after insults. Chat only. False keeps today's bots.
Server life: when you or a bot gains a level, groupmates say grats in /group and bots nearby in /say, and a realm's bots cheer a new level 50 in /faction.

Server life: the first character on the server (you or a bot) to reach level 50, the first of each class to reach 50 and the first to each realm rank from 2 up are announced to everyone and recorded for the Camelot Herald.

Server life: a bot that dies near you asks you for a rez if your class can rez, waits longer for it and thanks you after; a bot healer that is not in your group may rez you (you still accept or decline); bots talk about corpse runs and resurrection sickness.
Server life: a bot in the frontier that sees 3 or more enemies calls it out in /faction (rough size, classes, place), at most one call per realm every 2 minutes.

Server life: a bot killed by an enemy remembers its killer, names it (by race and class) in /faction after the second kill, and celebrates when it kills that enemy back. Kills are recorded for the Camelot Herald's Most Wanted.

Server life: autonomous gamebots standing around in town, waiting for their group or resting look around, emote now and then (ponder, shrug, laugh, stretch their legs with a step or two in town), turn and wave at you when you walk up, and cheer when someone dings nearby. Only where a real player can see it; never in a fight. Bots cannot jump or sit (the game sends no such state for them).
Bot defenders a siege may draw, as a share of its attacker cap (128 keep / 240 relic); walls, doors and keep guards are extra. Recent results move it up or down by up to 0.25 (SiegeDefenseBalance).

Automatic realm raids (dragons, epic dungeons, Summoner's Hall, Darkness Falls): level-50 bots that must be staged before the raid goes in. 0 (default) = half the realm's online level-50 bots, at least 40 and at most the encounter's suggested 200. Forced raids are unchanged.
Each realm opens an automatic realm raid on this schedule, rotating dragon, epic dungeon and neutral raid (0 = no schedule: raids only start when an eight-bot party happens to choose one).

Optional XP rate by level range for real player characters, for example 1-19:3;20-34:5;35-50:12. Inside a listed range its rate replaces xp_rate; other levels keep xp_rate. RvR zones keep rvr_zones_xp_rate. Empty (the default) or an invalid value keeps the flat xp_rate.

Optional XP rate by level range for autonomous gamebots, for example 1-19:1.5;20-34:2.5;35-50:6. Inside a listed range its rate replaces bot_xp_rate; other levels keep bot_xp_rate. In RvR zones the result is still multiplied by rvr_zones_xp_rate, as bot_xp_rate is. Empty (the default) or an invalid value keeps the flat bot_xp_rate. Companion bots and real players are not affected.
Share (0 to 1) of eligible autonomous gamebots that bot guild formation places in guilds.
Lowest level at which an autonomous gamebot is placed in a bot guild.
When bot guilds are on: guild members greet, congratulate and chat in guild chat when a real member can hear, answer your /gu, and bot guild officers recruit in /faction.
When bot guild social life is on: bot guild officers may invite you to their guild with a yes/no dialog (when you ask for a guild, or now and then when you are nearby and unguilded).

When bot guilds are on: after a realm takes a keep or tower, a bot guild with enough members inside claims it (claim_num, half for towers; guilds_claim_limit), never while a real player of that realm is inside. Its warbands answer first when that keep is attacked.

When bot guilds are on: guilded gamebots pay their guild's dues from the real coin they loot, their level-ups earn the guild merit points as a player's do, and bot guild leaders spend 1,000 merit points on a 24-hour guild buff.

When bot guilds are on: each realm's RvR and raiding bot guilds form one alliance (up to four guilds); a player in one of them hears its alliance chat. Alliances with a player's guild are never touched.
When bot voices are on: bots of a realm play the corpus's debates and long threads in /faction while you are online, one at a time, 30-45 minutes apart, never repeating a scene until all have played.

Server life: when autonomous gamebots are online. off = the whole roster (today's behavior); session = each bot plays sessions of 1-4 hours with 20 minutes to 2 hours away, timed from server start; clock = your PC's time of day (busiest 7-11pm and weekends, quiet overnight).

Server life: an idle bot now and then says brb and logs off for 5-25 minutes, and a bot grouped with you rarely goes linkdead for 30-90 seconds (the group hears about it) and comes back with an apology. Never during a fight, siege or relic march.
